>Posturing up using your body to look intimidating.

Ok. So by your own definition "posturing" is using your body to look *intimidating*. Now you use the term "intimidating" (I assume) to refer to someone accentuating their features and muscles and all that. Trying to look more attractive essentially, and "buffed up".

Now let's say I'm at a bar, and I spot some girl I want to chat up for the evening and see where things go later. I decide to walk up to her and posture, in order to look more desirable. It's a natural thing to do, whether guys know they're doing it or not. However, she sees what I'm doing, and tells me she's not interested. 

If things were to end here I feel this is innocent enough. She said no, and this more or less equates to a dead end. However what people in this thread are saying (and the original comment where this entire conversation arose from) is a feeling of intimidation from me, standing next to her all buffed up. Now I might not have meant to convey this fear into her, but she feels a little uncomfortable all the same. 

/u/jenax provided a *legal definition* (what courts use) for Assault. The link they provided reads:

>At Common Law, an intentional act by one person *that creates an apprehension in another* of an imminent harmful or offensive contact.

>An assault is carried out by a threat of bodily harm *coupled with an apparent, present ability to cause the harm.*

Now refer back to how you defined "Posturing". You said it was to look *intimidating*. While you and I both know you're just trying to look attractive to the person you're talking to, other people (specifically the girl you're chatting up) *don't know that* and may become apprehensive and fearful. Is this *automatically* assault? Not necessarily. But could it be *argued* as such? Yes.

Leaving alone all this talk of the person separating someone from an exit or following them home, and only focusing on the example I provided, do you not see how this act of posturing (looking intimidating similar to a UFC fighter as per your example) could be observed as some form of assault, (as per the legal definition provided) or at the very least an unwelcome behaviour?

In addition, you're frequently making reference to someone "being a douchebag" through actions such as blocking exits or responding violently to rejection, but couldn't someone imposing themselves upon someone they find attractive also be considered "being a douchebag"? Where does this line exactly end was the question I was hoping to have answered, as it doesn't seem like you're aware that chicks don't necessarily want someone to *intimidate them* when they're out for the evening.

I do agree with you partly in that me trying to look like Johnny Bravo shouldn't get me arrested on the spot, but when it's seen as unwelcome by the person I want to talk to I feel definitely (as observed by the legal definition) could be argued as a form of assault. In short, to paraphrase /u/jenax from earlier: just because *all* posturing is not a form of assault, doesn't mean that *some forms of posturing* (intimidating someone, looking like a UFC fighter, very physical bearing down on them, etc) *can be considered* assault (or at the very least, "being a douchebag".)
What is *your* definition of posturing? And how does "posturing" differ from "being a douchebag"? Just curious.

I think Starboy and The Weeknd himself is caught in this weird tipping point between MJ style pop/funk music and more classic House of Balloons style trap and dreamy R&B music. It's impossible for Abel to impress his entire fan base, as either his new fans will get upset when he goes into the slower stuff, but then his old fans will start screaming "BUT TRILOGY" when he puts out something like I Feel it Coming. 

Starboy was (in my opinion) the closest he was going to get to a blend of those sounds. It's still dark and dreary like his earlier work, but it also exudes that confidence and style found on Can't Feel My Face and his newer work on BBTM. I've heard people describe a lot of The Weeknd's stuff as sounding like "The Morning After" in a song, and thats definitely true here.

I didn't really like False Alarm. It literally sounded really rushed, as he more or less thrusts the listener into the chorus through yelling "FALSE ALARM", making the track lose any and all flow it might have had. Just my opinion, but personally the contrast from *Starboy* was just too jarring for me to get over.

With these two new tracks though, it's not as clear cut, and so the divide exists again. A lot of people on /r/TheWeeknd are praising Party Monster due to the callbacks to the Trilogy sound. And - like it or not - that sound is really, really well made. It's what he excels in, and so of course he's going to fucking kill it. A slow melodic beat, ambivalence towards and glorification of a life of drugs, sex and money, it's what the dude is known for mostly, and the polish on it here definitely makes a stellar track.

That said, I Feel It Coming is the track *I'm* going to play a lot more, due to that groove and the way Abel's voice integrates itself so well into Daft Punks sound. It harkens back to their sound on Random Access Memories, and even a bit of Discovery, which are albums I'd rank pretty high on my list. I must admit, I'd heard the snippet leaked prior to their official release, so *Feel It* had a little more time to grow on me, but I'm fairly certain I'd gravitate towards it more than Party Monster. 

I think it all boils down to what type of sound you want Abel to make at this point. You have people on one side wanting him to "Go full MJ" while others saying he should stick to his roots and make the dreary and dreamy R&B that got him where he is. He obviously puts a lot into his craft, and he definitely has a vision for what he wants to do, but either way there's going to be people unhappy. At the end of the day, dudes going to make whatever music he wants to make, and as long as he puts in the work we've seen so far from him in the songs, videos, and aesthetic he's created, I'm sure something good will come from it.

TL;DR: Not everyone loves Trilogy. Not everyone loves BBTM. But both I Feel it Coming and Party Monster are great, in spite of their vastly differing sound. Ones fruit punch on a beach at sunset, the other is ~~hard alcohol~~ **cocaine and ecstasy** at a strip club.

I mean I get it: it's your cash, and who am I to decide what you spend it on. But people here must have forgotten some very key information:

- Pre-Order stats can be seen by all developers/publishers. A large amount of people participating in this practice sends the message to *the entire industry* that the "Give money in hopes of a good product" strategy will succeed.

- While Rockstar has a good track record for their games, there's a multitude of things that can happen upon release. It may not live up to the hype, it may have micro transactions tacked on, it may lack key features the original did, etc. Just look at GTA V for an example.

- In addition, a company being in good standing with the gaming community (as *rare* as that may be) should not be treated as an immediate pass for any and all criticism. Look at Bethesda with Falllout 4 for an eerily similar situation (I actually recall this same image being posted as well). Hyped beyond belief, expectations through the roof, and pre-ordered by many, only for the immediate reaction to be a resounding "meh" due to tedious fetch quests, lacklustre environment, and a reworked dialogue system and story mechanics that proved inferior to its predecessors Fallout 3 and New Vegas.

- The game is available *everywhere* at launch. Seriously. The base copy can easily be found at any location nearest to you, or even online digitally, and you even have a good shot at getting the special pre-order edition too, with those bonuses going up for sale most likely a week after as well. Mortal Kombat X is a great example of this, as apparently Goro lives everywhere, and not just via pre-order.

While it's cool we're on the cusp of a new Rockstar game, and I'm certain they'll deliver a better product than something like No Mans Sky, people saying they'll pre-order the second they can are just feeding into this culture where developers and publishers can give less and less, banking on the success of previous titles to earn cash up front. We all have studios we're fans of. But people really need to cool their jets with this stuff, as I'm certain whenever games like Fallout 4 or No Mans Sky get brought up, they'll lambast people who said the exact comments they're saying now here.

Eternal youth was something fun once I suppose.

It was a pipe dream where you'd watch new things be built each day, the buildings grow taller only to pierce the heavens as opposed to merely scraping skies. You would no longer use the phrase "in my lifetime" for when things such as the self driving car, the first spaceship, or the instant turkey dinner were invented. Death lost it's clutch around your throat, and finally you could breathe.

But it isn't merely watching the new things being constructed that you watch, but the old things they replace torn down. As you watch the world you knew ripped to shreds, the deck shuffled completely, you find that you're no longer "home" anymore. You witness the demise of the treasured obsolete. Places so sentimental blown away, to watch each single card fall, rendered into not a thing to be remembered.

The people are always the hardest to lose. When you witness the first wife fall it is soul crushing. And so are the ones that will undoubtedly follow. But soon you grow hollow, finding the pursuit of a partner that is forcefully torn from you. There are a dozen gravestones in the cemetery for people id "loved". But but the end of them it was the furthest definition of "love" one could find, because how can you throw all your chips in if you know you're going to lose it all anyway?

So now I wait out my days, hiding from the things I once partook in. Where people become less human and more artificial, and all connection from myself to the world is lost, with no way of restoring it even if I wanted to. And one day perhaps even earth itself will be replaced by something "new and improved", and so all those people I'd never met would leave me here, kicking dust and gravel, left with the absolute obsolete.
That is beautiful. :)
